summary: In 2020 I was brought into Instapage to build what came next: Postclick. Landing pages at scale, built entirely through ML and the early glimpses of AI. The product couldn't do what we promised, so I threw people at the gap, using humans to replicate what the AI wasn't ready to do. It taught me something I've never forgotten: the right idea at the wrong time never gets wings, and category creation breaks companies. When I took over as CEO, everything was fractured. A founder and my predecessor out of sync. A board split on what came next. A company that had lost its north star, sold on a deal that was quietly bleeding it dry while revenue and morale fell together. So I did the hard work. Three reductions in force. Rebuilt the cost structure. Got people mission-aligned and re-engaged around the legacy business. I reset the deal terms everyone had given up on and ran the sale to an $80M exit, even knowing I wouldn't be part of the chapter that followed. Here's what stayed with me. The thing that nearly killed that company wasn't product or market. It was people out of sync, and nobody could see it until the damage was done. I could not unsee it. So I built Hatchproof. "Hatchproof helped us see misalignment early, before it turned into churn or drama. It changed how I think about performance, not as a review cycle, but as something you can manage in real time." Greg Chen, CEO, Mobiz Hatchproof reads the real signal in how teams work, through 1:1s, Slack, your CRM and HRIS, and shows you who's at risk, who drives value, and where teams fall out of sync. Moneyball, sitting next to your revenue dashboard. Built with a Chief Scientist from Harvard, design partners like IBM, backed by Techstars NYC. From San Francisco. summary: Three decades in contact centers taught me one thing. Every technology wave promised better customer conversations and delivered cheaper ones. IVR. Chatbots. Self-service portals. Who are your best agents, the ones customers ask for by name, the ones who turn complaints into loyalty, and what exactly are they doing on the call? That question built BrainCX. We ingest recorded calls from a client's top performers and clone the attributes that make them exceptional. Voice. Tone. Pace. Empathy. Objection handling. The science of human communication, deployed at scale across voice, chat, web, and avatar. One platform. Every channel. While the AI talks, our platform surfaces the right images, pricing, and forms on the website in real time. Voice and visual move together. No competitor does this. This platform is patent-pending. The results follow from the method. After more than 100K+ calls, less than 1% of callers ever asked if they were speaking with an AI. Not one asked to be transferred to a human. I co-founded Firstsource, India's first publicly traded BPO. I served as Chief Country Officer at JPMorgan in the Philippines, where our team became the country's largest private employer and earned a J.D. Power Award. I led global support for Apple across six countries. Every role, every continent, every failed deployment pointed at the same gap. BrainCX closes it. If you run a contact center in healthcare, behavioral health, higher education, travel, or financial services, let's talk. https://braincx.ai/tariq
job description: I founded BrainCX on a single conviction: off-the-shelf AI breaks in high-trust environments, and the industry has been asking the wrong question. Every contact center technology wave — IVR, chatbots, self-service — was built around cost reduction. We built around a different question: who are your best agents, and what exactly are they doing on the call? BrainCX ingests recorded calls from a client's top performers and clones the attributes that make them exceptional — voice, tone, pace, empathy, objection handling. The result is a patent-pending platform that deploys the science of human communication at scale across voice, chat, web, and avatar. While the AI talks, our platform simultaneously surfaces the right images, pricing, and forms on the client's website in real time. Voice and visual move together. No competitor does this. The platform is live with enterprise clients across healthcare, financial services, and higher education — sectors where one bad interaction creates compliance risk, churn, or both. After more than 100,000 calls, less than 1% of callers ever asked if they were speaking with an AI. Not one asked to be transferred to a human. BrainCX is generating recurring revenue and growing quarter over quarter.

job description (2): Spirit was growing faster than its service infrastructure could handle. I was brought in to close that gap. In under three years, guest satisfaction moved from 60% to 90%. That number didn't come from a rebranding exercise. It came from rebuilding how the operation worked at every layer: technology, vendor structure, agent tools, and digital channels. When the pandemic hit, we had days to respond. Millions of guests needed to cancel, rebook, or get refunds simultaneously. Instead of collapsing under call volume, we deployed an asynchronous digital messaging strategy that automated millions of transactions without friction. Spirit's cost base held. Guest trust held. Most carriers couldn't say the same. I restructured the outsourcing model using a champion-challenger framework. Vendors compete for volume based on performance, not tenure. That single structural change drove down cost, drove up quality, and gave us leverage we didn't have before. I also led the deployment of AI, bots, and human-augmented channels across multiple locations. Not as a cost play, but as an agent enablement play. The best outcomes came when technology removed the cognitive load from agents and let them focus on the calls that actually required a human. The lesson I carried out of Spirit: you can transform a high-volume, low-trust service environment into a high-performance one without replacing your people. You replace the broken system around them.

job description (4): After running large operations inside institutions, I spent two years on the outside looking in, advising enterprise clients on the global outsourcing decisions that most companies get wrong. The typical failure pattern: a company picks a geography based on labor cost, selects a vendor based on a proposal, and discovers six months later that the cultural fit, the quality infrastructure, and the management overhead were never accounted for. I built frameworks that fixed that sequence before it started. Clients included Fortune 500 brands expanding into Asia, Latin America, and EMEA, and high-growth companies that needed to scale service operations faster than they could hire domestically. For each, I designed the vendor selection model, the geographic rationale, the performance governance structure, and the transition plan. One of the more consequential engagements was building a strategic alliance between a large US healthcare enterprise and an India-based revenue cycle management partner. Claims accuracy improved. Processing speed improved. The operational cost reduction was significant. More importantly, the partnership held, which is rarer than most people admit in this industry. This period sharpened something I had been building across my entire career: a clear view of where outsourcing creates genuine competitive advantage and where it creates the illusion of savings while destroying customer trust. That distinction is what I brought to BrainCX.
